questions.question: Which of the following events occurred before the arrival of Simon Commission in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kakori Conspiracy**__.

__
 
• **The Kakori conspiracy took place before the arrival of the Simon Commission in India.**
 
• The Kakori Train Action was **a train robbery, carried out on August 9, 1925, by the revolutionaries of the Indian independence movement against the British Raj in a village called Kakori near Lucknow.**
 
• This robbery was carried out by **10 revolutionaries including Hindustan Republican Association's revolutionary Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaq Ullah Khan, Rajendra Lahiri, Keshav Chakraborty, Mukundi Lal and Banwari Lal.**
 
• Significantly, **freedom fighters Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaq Ullah Khan and Roshan Singh were hanged on 19 December 1927 for their involvement in the Kakori conspiracy.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **The First Round Table Conference**

 
 
• **​The first Round Table Conference started on 12 November 1930 in London.**
 
• During this time, the independence movement in India was in full swing and there were **constant demands for the grant of Dominion status to India.**
 
 
 
• **Gandhi-Irwin Pact**
 
 
• **​A political pact was signed by Mahatma Gandhi and the then Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin, before the Second Round Table Conference in London on 5 March 1931.**
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement**
 
 
• **​**The Quit India Movement was **a civil disobedience movement in India launched in August 1942 in response to Mahatma Gandhi's call for India's immediate independence.**

questions.question: Who among the following introduced the ’Doctrine of Lapse’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The doctrine of lapse, **a formula formulated by Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India (1848–56), to deal with questions of succession in Hindu Indian states.**
 
• According to this policy,** if the king did not have any natural-born heir then the kingdom would lapse to the British or would be administered and occupied by the British.**
 
• Indian states such as **Satara, Nagpur and Jhansi were annexed under this policy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Dalhousie**

 
 
• **​**On 12 January 1848,** he was appointed Governor-General of India and Governor of Bengal**.
 
• Dalhousie considered **the consolidation of British power in India **as its main objective.
 
• He was responsible for introducing many modern reforms in India **such as railways, telegraph and postal networks and public works.​**
 
• ​​He is best remembered for** the Doctrine of Lapse Policy, which many attributes directly to the Indian Rebellion of 1857.**
 
• Lord Dalhousie also started many **Anglo-vernacular schools in India**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Ripon**
 
 
• **​**Viceroy of India from 1880-84.
 
• **The Vernacular Press Act was cancelled in 1882**.
 
• The first Factory Act was implemented in 1881.
 
 
 
• **Warren Hastings**
 
 
• ​First Governor of the Presidency of Fort Williams.
 
• **First Governor-General of Bengal.**
 
• Warren Hastings played an important role in the **abolition of dual system.**
 
• To collect the **revenue a Board of Revenue was set up at Calcutta**.

questions.question: What are the two different scripts and languages in which the Kandahar Bilingual Rock Inscriptions were written?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greek and Aramaic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kandahar bilingual inscription**

 
 
• The Kandahar bilingual inscription is a famous bilingual inscription in **Greek and Aramaic**.
 
• Declared and carved **around 260 BC by Ashoka, the ruler of the Indian Maurya Empire.**
 
• ​This is the **earliest known inscription of Ashoka, written in the 10th year of his reign**.
 
• **This first inscription was written exclusively in Classical Greek and Aramaic.**
 
• It was **discovered in 1958, during some excavation work under a 1-meter-high layer of rubble, and is known as KAI 279**.
 
• It is sometimes **considered one of Ashoka's many "Minor Rock Edicts", in contrast to his "Major Rock Edicts", which consist of portions or totality of his Edicts from 1 to 14.**
 
• Two inscriptions have been found in Afghanistan with Greek inscriptions, one of which is a bilingual inscription in Greek and Aramaic, the other being a Kandahar Greek inscription only in Greek.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aramaic and Greek**

 
 
• ​A bilingual Ashokan inscription, inscribed in Greek and Aramaic, is found at Kandhar.
 
 
 
• **Persian and Arabic ​**
 
 
• Arabic & Persian Inscriptions were found in the 14th-century mosque in Dholka Gujarat, India.

questions.question: Which of the following is a conventional source of energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Firewood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sources of Energy**

 
 
• **​Two major sources of energy are classified as Conventional and Non-Conventional Sources.**
 
 
 
• **Conventional Sources of Energy**
 
 
• **​**Conventional Sources of Energy are also **known as non-renewable sources of energy and are available in limited quantity apart from hydroelectric power**.
 
• They serve **both commercial and industrial purposes.**
 
• These can be** considered as one of the causes of pollution.**
 
• In addition,** it is classified under commercial and non-commercial energy.**
 
• **Commercial Energy- Coal, electricity and petroleum**.
 
• **Non-commercial Energy- straw, dried dung, firewood.**
 
 
 
• **Non-Conventional Sources of Energy**
 
 
• **​Non-conventional sources are also known as renewable sources of energy.**
 
• These are **mainly used for domestic purposes.**
 
• They are **not responsible for the causes of pollution**.
 
• Examples of non-conventional sources of energy include** solar energy, bioenergy, tidal energy and wind power.**

questions.question: The aim of ________ is to promote the Panchayati Raj Institutions in the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seventy-third Amendment Act, 1992**

 
 
• **​In 1992, the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act was passed, and it came into effect on April 24, 1993.**
 
• The Act empowered the state governments **to formalize village panchayats and adopt necessary procedures to enable them to function as autonomous bodies.**
 
• This act added a** new Part-IX to the Indian Constitution.**
 
• This section is titled **'The Panchayats' and it contains provisions from Articles 243 to 243 O.**
 
• In addition, the Act added** a new Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution**.
 
• **There are 29 Panchayat functional items included in this schedule. It is related to Article 243-G.**
 
 
 
• **Objective**
 
 
• **​Democratic decentralization of power and resources from the centre to elected representatives at lower levels to allow individuals to participate more directly in governance.**
 
• The object of the 73rd amendment** pertains to Article 40 of the Constitution which requires the state to organize village panchayats and provide them with the necessary powers and authority to function as units of self-government.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Sixtieth Amendment Act, 1988**

 
 
• **​**Article 276 of the Constitution relating to **taxes on professions, professions, occupations and employment was amended.**
 
 
 
• **Forty-third Amendment Act, 1977**
 
 
• **​Restored the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and the high courts in respect of judicial review and issue of writs.**
 
 
 
• **Thirty-Seventh Amendment Act, 1975**
 
 
• **​Parliament passed it on April 26, 1975, to make way for a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers for Arunachal Pradesh, the north-Easternmost Union territory of the country.**

questions.question: Which process is used by the unicellular freshwater organisms and most plant cells to take in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Osmosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unicellular freshwater organisms and most plant cells tend to gain water through osmosis**.
 
• The absorption of water by plant roots is also an example of osmosis.
 
• Osmosis can be defined as **the spontaneous movement of solvent molecules through a semi-permeable membrane, from a low-concentration solution to a high-concentration solution.**
 
• Osmosis is purely a mechanical process where cells absorb water without spending any amount of energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morphogenesis**

 
 
• ​**A biological process that causes a tissue or organ to develop its shape by controlling the spatial distribution of cells during embryonic development.**
 
 
 
• **Hybridisation**
 
 
• **​A process of mathematically combining two or more atomic orbitals from the same atom to form a completely different orbital from its constituents** is therefore called a hybrid orbital.
 
 
 
• **Tropism**
 
 
• **​The growth rate of plant parts in which the direction of stimulus determines the direction of response is called tropism.**
 
• Example: **Phototropism, where plant stems grow upward in response to sunlight.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the successor of Chandragupta I?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Samudragupta (335AD-380 AD)**__

 __
 
• **​**Chandragupta I, **was succeeded by his son Samudragupta.**
 
• Samudragupta was the **greatest king of the Gupta dynasty**.
 
• The most detailed and **authentic record of his reign is preserved in the Prayaga Prasasti/Allahabad pillar inscription, composed by his court poet Harisena.**
 
• Samudragupta’s **military campaigns justify the description of him as the Napoleon of India by V.A. Smith**.
 
• Titles:** Kaviraja, Param Bhagavat, Ashvamedha- parikrama, Vikram Sarva-rajochchhetta only Gupta ruler had the title of Sarva-raj-ochchhetta.**
 
• **Allahabad pillar inscriptions mention the title Dharma Prachar Bandhu, i.e. he was the upholder of Brahmanical religion.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta II **

 
 
• Chandragupta II, also called Vikramaditya, powerful emperor (reigned c. 380–c. 415 ce) of northern India.
 
 
 
• **Ghatotkacha **
 
 
• Ghatotkacha was the second ruler of the Gupta Dynasty. He was the successor of his father Sri Gupta. He ruled between 280 AD to 319 AD.
 
 
 
• **Vikramaditya**
 
 
• Vikramaditya ruled over parts of India in the 1st century BCE, and popular culture credits him with starting the Vikrama Samvat era in 57 BCE.

• **Devprayag**

 
 
• Devprayag is **a town and a Nagar panchayat (municipality) in Tehri Garhwal district in the state of Uttarakhand, India.**
 
• **It is one of the Panch Prayag (five confluences) of the Alaknanda River where the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi rivers meet and take the name Ganga.**
 
• According to mythology, there is another river related to this confluence named Saraswati, which originates from Mana village of Badrinath.

• **Ghaghara**

 
 
• **​**Ghaghara River is a tributary of** Ganga River**.
 
• This river originates in the Tibetan Plateau near** Lake Mansarovar**.
 
 
 
• **Gandak**
 
 
• Gandak River, also called **Narayani River**, river in central Nepal and northern India.
 
• It is formed by the union of the** Kali** and **Trisuli rivers**.
 
 
 
• **Meghna**
 
 
• **​**The combined flow of the Ganga (the Padma in Bangladesh), the **Barak river **and the Jamuna river are known as **Meghna **in** Bangladesh**.
